titleBar.ordinanceTitle: Village ordinance (rules shared by all servants)
titleBar.commandApprovalTitle: Approve or reject commands requested by servants

settings.title: System settings

theme.heading: Theme
theme.intro: Choose the colour scheme. It switches the moment you pick one.
theme.darkNote: Light text on a dark ground. Suits dim rooms and long sessions.
theme.lightNote: Dark text on a light ground. Suits bright rooms and working alongside documents.
theme.deviceNote: The theme is stored on this device. Until you choose, it follows your OS setting.

settings.villageScope: This setting is stored in the village configuration (world.json), so it travels with the village when you share it.

user.heading: User
user.help: Your own name and icon. The name is included in the messages servants read, and is also your display name on screen.
user.nameHint: Servants address you by this name. Leave it empty to fall back to the default ("You"). Up to 32 characters; the character 】 and line breaks are not allowed.
user.iconRemoveMessage: The chat pane falls back to a circle with your initial.

tokenBudget.heading: Token limit (effective tokens)
tokenBudget.help: The sum of uncached ×1 + cached ×0.1 + output ×4. Managed internally in milli units; displayed as a rounded-up integer. When a single request's token spend reaches this value, the request is cut off automatically.
tokenBudget.invalid: Enter an integer of 1 or more (0 cannot remove the limit — choose "No limit" instead).
tokenBudget.guideline: Guide: village of ~6 = 1,000,000 / 12-servant scale or output-heavy code generation = 2,000,000–3,000,000
tokenBudget.noCeilingWarning: In a village without a limit, a single request keeps burning tokens when a failure loop occurs. Setting a limit is recommended.
tokenBudget.saved: Saved. Takes effect from the next request (no restart needed).

language.heading: Language
language.help: Display language of the UI. The switch takes effect the moment you save.
language.promptNote: Instructions to servants (system prompts and tool descriptions) are not translated — translating them would change the prompts. System lines in the conversation log stay in the language they were written in.

messages.heading: Message visibility
messages.intro: Confirmations and notices that can be suppressed are collected here.
messages.instantNote: Changes are saved immediately, on this machine only (not part of the village configuration).

edgeDelete.heading: Cutting a tie
edgeDelete.intro: In Kizuna, clicking a tie cuts it. A cut tie cannot be restored.
edgeDelete.checkbox: Show a confirmation dialog before deleting
edgeDelete.offWarning: While confirmation is off, a single click on a tie cuts it.

closeWindow.heading: Closing the window
closeWindow.intro: This app does not stay in the tray. Closing it stops the servants and the schedules.
closeWindow.offWarning: While confirmation is off, one click on the close button quits.

presence.heading: Join and leave notices
presence.intro: Whether servants starting and stopping show up in the chat pane. This is a display setting only; it does not change what servants receive.
presence.checkbox: Show join and leave notices in the chat pane
presence.failureNote: Stops caused by a failure are always shown, whatever this is set to. The servant list only shows the current state, so the chat pane is the only place a past failure leaves a trace.

mcpHost.heading: MCP server (accept requests from external LLMs)
mcpHost.lead: Lets MCP clients such as Claude Code send a single request to this village. The reception servant receives it and returns a consolidated answer.
mcpHost.enableHint: Disabled by default. A token is generated when you enable it.
mcpHost.portHint: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only (other machines cannot connect).
mcpHost.tokenHint: Paste this into your client configuration. Any process that knows this value can send requests to the village.
mcpHost.tokenNotYet: Not generated yet (enabling the server creates one)
mcpHost.regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the token? Clients configured with the current value will stop connecting.
mcpHost.receptionHint: The servant that first receives external requests. While unset, requests are answered with that reason.
mcpHost.concurrencyNote: Only one request is processed at a time. A second request while busy is refused immediately rather than queued.
mcpHost.scopeNote: These settings are stored on this machine (they do not travel with a copied village). Only the reception is stored in the village.
mcpHost.identityHint: The name and icon shown in the conversation pane. Setting a name also changes the sender name servants read (otherwise the client’s self-declared name is used).
mcpHost.externalNamePlaceholder: Not set (use the client’s declared name)
mcpHost.externalNameHint: Up to 32 characters. Takes effect from the next turn (past conversation logs are not rewritten).

grounding.heading: Grounding
grounding.sourcesMissing: No sources were returned (URLs in the reply are not confirmed citations).

agentList.heading: Servants
agentList.batchAllTransitioning: All targets are currently changing state
agentList.batchNoTargets: No servants are selected for batch start (choose with the toggle on each card)
agentList.noTemplates: No model templates are registered. Register one first via the "Manage model templates" button above.
agentList.emptyLine2: Add one with the + button in the top right.

agentCard.batchIncluded: Included in batch start (▶). Click to exclude
agentCard.batchExcluded: Excluded from batch start (▶). Click to include
agentCard.cacheDetail: Total {total} ({input} input / {output} output; output is {outputShare}% of the total). {cached} of the input tokens were read from the prompt cache. Output cannot be cached, so the rate is relative to input (0% means the cache is not being hit)

chatInput.hint: Enter to send / Shift+Enter for a new line
chatInput.attachNote: This image is sent to the model for this turn only. From the next turn on, the model cannot see it (it stays visible here).
chatInput.attachScaled: Scaled down to {px}px on the long edge.
chatInput.attachConvertedTooLarge: The converted image is too large (limit: 2MB)
chatInput.completeNoWorkDir: This servant has no work folder set, so file completion is unavailable.
chatInput.completeFailed: Could not load the file list.
chatInput.completeTruncated: The candidate list hit its limit. Some files are not shown here.
chatInput.clearView: Clear the chat view (display only — the conversation stays, and servants still receive it)

bottomTabs.blackboardTitle: The village blackboard (shared working notes). Shows the 黒板/ folder under work_dir; nothing can be written from here
bottomTabs.wavesTitle: Execution traces of plan. Columns = waves / rows = servants

blackboard.refreshTitle: Reload the blackboard (it also refreshes automatically while shown)
blackboard.empty: Nothing has been written on the blackboard yet (notes placed in the 黒板/ folder under work_dir will appear here).

map.heading: Kizuna
map.headingHelp: Drag a handle to form a tie / click a tie to cut it (a bidirectional tie cuts both ways)
map.bidirectionalNote: This is a bidirectional tie, so both directions will be cut.
map.autoFit: Fit automatically after the pane is resized

chat.heading: Chat
chat.newChatTitle: Close this conversation and start a new one (the previous conversation is saved and can be reopened from the session list)
chat.newChatConfirmTitle: Close this conversation and start a new one?
chat.newChatConfirmMessage: The current conversation is saved, and you can return to it anytime from Sessions.
chat.sessionsTitle: Saved conversations. Reopen, fork, export, or delete
chat.summarizeTitle: Summarizes the conversation so far to shorten future prompts (applies to running servants; uses tokens; the original exchanges are not lost)
chat.summarizeConfirmTitle: Summarize the conversation so far and continue?
chat.summarizeConfirmMessage:
This calls the model once per running servant, so it uses tokens (stopped servants are skipped).
The original exchanges are not lost (you can read them via the export in Sessions).
chat.interruptAllTitle: Interrupts all in-flight turns (servants stay running; the conversation and history are kept)
chat.toolOkTitle: Whether the tool returned an error, not whether the side effect succeeded
chat.interruptTurnTitle: Interrupts {name}'s current turn (the servant stays running; the conversation and history are kept)
chat.interruptPending: Stop requested… (it will stop once the current operation finishes)
chat.attachmentDeleted: This image was deleted after its retention period
chat.clearedNote: Earlier messages hidden: {count} (the conversation is still there)

editor.mcpPlaceholder: JSON in the same mcpServers format as Claude Desktop. Leave it empty if this servant has no dedicated MCP. Broken JSON cannot be saved.
editor.markdownPlaceholder: Written in Markdown. If you save it empty, this section is not included in the prompt.
editor.discardSwitchMessage: Your edits will not be saved.
editor.runPlaceholder:
Only calls matching allow are executed; deny wins over allow.
Calls in neither list are recorded under pending — move them to allow or deny here.
A trailing * means "any remaining arguments"; a pattern without * matches only a call with no arguments.
This is not a safety mechanism: allowing a command permits everything that command can do.

{'{'}
  "version": 1,
  "allow": ["ruff *", "cargo test *"],
  "deny": [],
  "pending": [],
  "timeoutSecs": 60
{'}'}

ordinance.title: Village Ordinance
ordinance.discardCloseMessage: Your edits to the ordinance will not be saved.
ordinance.description: These are {rules}. They sit at the top of every servant's system prompt (above individual settings) and take effect from the next message after saving. You can also write shared rules here to even out behavioral differences between models.
ordinance.descriptionRules: rules that apply to every servant in this village
ordinance.placeholder:
Example:
This is Outcasts Village.
- Value implementation details and verifiable claims over vague impressions
- End the conversation rather than repeating what someone said
- Polite but frank; no flattery

mcp.title: MCP Servers
mcp.discardCloseMessage: Your edits will not be saved.
mcp.description: Connect external tools via {mcp} (Model Context Protocol). The format is {sameAs}, so you can paste an existing configuration {asIs} (commands such as `npx` are resolved from PATH). Saving reconnects immediately, and each servant can use the tools from its next message. {secrets} — this file is stored in plain text.
mcp.descriptionSecrets: Do not write secrets such as API keys here
mcp.editorPlaceholder: (not configured) Start from the Example button at the top right
mcp.saveNote: Saving reconnects the servers (no app restart needed)

uiErrors.canvasContext: Could not get a canvas 2D context

agentSettings.openFolderFailed: Could not open the configuration folder
agentSettings.iconHint: Pick a png / jpg and it will be converted to WebP and saved.
agentSettings.iconRemoveMessage: The avatar reverts to the round initial.
agentSettings.name: Name
agentSettings.workDir: Working folder (search scope for grep / diff)
agentSettings.workDirPlaceholder: e.g. D:\Projects\my-app (tools stay inactive until set)
agentSettings.workDirHint: Bundled tools can read only inside this folder. Do not point it at folders containing secrets.
agentSettings.maxToolsHint: How many tool calls one response may use. For research-heavy coding servants, raising it to 12–20 makes truncation less likely (at the cost of more tokens).
agentSettings.toolsDefault: Default (all; new tools are added automatically)
agentSettings.noWorkDirWarn: No working folder is set, so file tools are not offered (your checkmarks are kept).
agentSettings.rememberOffWarn: Unchecking remember stops long-term memory from updating itself (Memory.md is still loaded).
agentSettings.hearsRoomLogHint: Conversations between other servants will no longer be available as context (this saves tokens). This servant's own remarks are still heard by the others as before.
agentSettings.mcpIdle: Stopped (not connected). Declarations can be edited in the mcp.json tab and connect on startup.
agentSettings.mcpEmpty: No per-servant server declarations (add them in the mcp.json tab).
agentSettings.ragEmpty: No reference folders are declared (without a declaration the rag tool is not offered).
agentSettings.ragHint: Declaring a folder automatically offers the rag tool, which reads its Markdown through a heading index (read-only; outside the working folder is allowed). Removing every folder removes the tool. Everything in a declared folder becomes readable by this servant, so do not declare folders containing secrets.
agentSettings.deleteMessage: Its configuration files (SKILL.md, Memory.md, mcp.json, icon) will also be removed. This cannot be undone.
agentSettings.discardMessage: Your edits will not be saved.
agentSettings.roleHelp: This changes only the role label. Settings (Construct.md, model, and so on) are copied at creation time, so changing the role here does not change them.
agentSettings.runOnWarn: Command execution is enabled. The work-folder limit does not constrain executed commands. Only calls matching the allow list in this servant's run.json (edited next to the mcp.json tab) can run. The tool is offered even while allow is empty, but nothing can be executed in that state — non-matching calls are recorded as pending, so approving one from "Command approval" in the title bar lets it pass from the next turn.

modelTemplate.title: Model templates
modelTemplate.idLockedHint: The identifier doubles as the credential key and as the reference servants point to, so it cannot be changed after creation.
modelTemplate.baseUrlMismatch: The selected protocol and the destination do not match. This configuration will always fail.
modelTemplate.keyPlaceholderStored: Paste a new key to overwrite
modelTemplate.keyStored: Registered. Stored in the OS credential store.
modelTemplate.keyMissing: No key registered. Requests will be rejected before sending as misconfigured and fall back to echo responses.
modelTemplate.authNotRequired: This endpoint needs no authentication (local inference server, etc.)
modelTemplate.toolCallsHint: When disabled, tool schemas are carried in the prompt instead
modelTemplate.googleSearchHint: Answers are grounded with Google Search first (can be combined with bundled tools and delegation)
modelTemplate.strandedStrong: it does nothing because the protocol is not Gemini
modelTemplate.strandedAfter: . Grounding exists only on the Gemini native path. To use it, set the protocol to Gemini native.
modelTemplate.keyStoreBefore: API keys are stored in the
modelTemplate.keyStoreAfter: (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service). They are never written to configuration files, and there is no way to read them back into this screen. Only whether a key is registered can be shown.
modelTemplate.noSelection: Select from the list on the left, or create a new one with ＋.
modelTemplate.deleteKeyMessage: It will be removed from the OS credential store. Servants using this template will no longer be able to connect.
modelTemplate.deleteTemplateMessage: Servants referencing this template will not run until they are given another model.
modelTemplate.xaiWebSearchHint: Searches the web before answering (source URLs are returned)
modelTemplate.xaiXSearchHint: Searches posts on X. Post URLs and real engagement counts come back, but what is returned is that something was posted — not that it is true
modelTemplate.xaiSearchCost: A turn that searches costs an order of magnitude more input tokens, because results are injected into the prompt (measured: 98,213, of which 62,720 cached). In a village with a small token limit, one search can exhaust it.
modelTemplate.strandedXaiStrong: it does nothing because the protocol is not xAI native (Responses)
modelTemplate.strandedXaiAfter: . Live Search exists only on the Responses path. To use it, set the protocol to "xAI native (Responses)".
modelTemplate.passivePromptCacheHint: Caches the shared preamble (ordinance, role, roster) for 1 hour, lowering input cost on later turns. Applies to requests above 2,048 tokens.

schedule.title: Schedules (timed requests)
schedule.noticeIntro: Delivers a fixed request to a servant at a fixed time. Results appear in the conversation pane.
schedule.noticeLimit: Schedules do not run while the app is closed.
schedule.noticeCatchUp: Missed schedules are not run retroactively (interval schedules run once after restart).
schedule.empty: No schedules yet. Use the form below to choose which servant, what request, and when.
schedule.noAgents: No servants are registered, so there is no one to address. Create a servant in the left pane first.
schedule.probeToggle: Check with a command before asking
schedule.probeHint: When the time comes, run a command first and only ask the servant if the first line of its output matches the signal. Runs that do not match cost no tokens at all.
schedule.probeExpectHint: Asks the servant when the first line of output equals this string. Any following lines are attached to the request (the exit code is not used for the decision).
schedule.probeUnapproved: This command is not approved on this machine yet. It will not run until you approve it.
schedule.approveConfirmMessage:
This lets the command below run on this machine. Read it before approving.

{command}
schedule.freshToggle: Start a new conversation each time
schedule.freshHint: The whole village switches to a new conversation. The previous one is kept and can be reopened from the conversation list.
schedule.summarizeHint: Summarises only the servants involved in this request. Summaries stay in every later turn (unlike a new conversation, they are not discarded).

session.title: Conversations
session.forkNoticeAfter: the chosen request, and puts that request's text back into the input box. Rewrite and send it to try a different phrasing. The original conversation is left untouched.
session.listNoticeIntro: Conversations persist across restarts. Reopen one and the servants answer with the earlier discussion in mind.
session.listNoticeLimit: Switching is only possible while no turn is in flight.
session.forkEmpty: There is nothing to fork from. Forking means going back to just before a request, so the very first request cannot be chosen (before it lies an empty conversation, which is the same as starting a new chat).
session.forkPointAction: Up to just before this request →
session.openTitle: Open this conversation (refused while a turn is in flight)
session.forkBtnTitle: Copy up to a point and try a different phrasing from there
session.exportTitle: Export as JSONL (the store is binary, so this is the readable way out)
session.deleteConfirmMessage: Its messages and histories cannot be recovered. If you want to keep it, export it first.

orchestrator.toolLimitDetail: Limit: {max} calls. Raise it in the servant settings or split the request into smaller pieces
orchestrator.repeatBlocked: {name} was cut off for repeating the same operation
orchestrator.repeatBlockedDetail: {tool} was called with the same arguments and returned the same result {repeats} times. The next call was not executed

statusBar.clockTitle: Current date and time (same format as the diagnostic log prefix)
statusBar.versionTitle: Version of this build (nearest git tag; 0.0.0 when untagged)
statusBar.mcpHostTitle: Accepting requests from external LLMs (127.0.0.1:{port}). Turn it off under Settings > Integration > MCP server when not in use.

roles.title: Roles
roles.help: Templates for creating servants. Pick a role when creating one and it starts with its settings already filled in. The role name appears as a badge on cards and in Kizuna.
roles.badgeTitle: This servant was created from the "{name}" template. It does not guarantee the current settings, which can be changed after creation.
roles.editNote: Editing here does not change servants that already exist, because settings are copied at creation time. Only the role name on the badge follows.
roles.confirmDeleteBody: Servants created from this role keep working unchanged, since their settings were copied at creation time. Only the role badge disappears.

fields.idHelp: Cannot be changed later. Letters, digits, - and _ are allowed.
fields.idInvalid: Use only letters, digits, - and _, up to 64 characters.
fields.name: Role name
fields.nameHelp: The name shown on badges and in the roster. Renaming it updates every display.
fields.descriptionHelp: For whoever picks a template on this screen. It is never sent to servants.
fields.colorHelp: Used for badges in the list and in Kizuna. Changing it applies immediately to every servant holding this role.

defaults.heading: Defaults applied when creating with this role
defaults.help: These values are applied to a new servant. Ties and the work folder are deliberately excluded: ties are formed by people, and the work folder differs per machine.

roles.villageScope: Roles are stored in the village (world.json), so they travel with it when shared.

commandApproval.title: Command Approval
commandApproval.help: Commands a servant tried to run and was refused. Choose what to permit, then approve or reject. Approved entries run directly from then on; rejected ones never appear here again.
commandApproval.broken: This servant's run.json cannot be read (it is not valid JSON). Fix it from the configuration files. The broken file has been left untouched.
commandApproval.gone: This request is no longer listed (newer requests pushed it out). Nothing was added to the permitted or forbidden lists.
commandApproval.presentNote: Once even one entry is permitted, that servant gains the command-running tool from its next turn. For finer control, edit run.json directly from the configuration files.

closeConfirm.title: Quit Fuseforks?
closeConfirm.lead: Nothing in this village runs while the app is closed.
closeConfirm.running: Turns in flight for {count} running servant(s) will be lost.
closeConfirm.mcp: The MCP server door closes (external requests stop arriving).
closeConfirm.schedules: Schedules will not fire — they only run while this app is open.

batchWorkDir.title: Change work folders together
batchWorkDir.intro: Sets the work folder of every checked servant to the path you enter. Running servants pick it up from their next message. Whether the folder exists is not checked here (you find out when a tool uses it).
